inputs.xtext_rule_text:
FilterPackage returns SysML::Package :
	ownedRelationship += FilterPackageImport
	( ownedRelationship += FilterPackageMember )+
;

decision: As KerML 8.2.3.4.2 states it: an ImportDeclaration, then one or more FilterPackageMembers, each a bracketed OwnedExpression. This is the KerML variant (ADR-0014); the SysML clause states the production differently, which is why it is split. The Xtext writes FilterPackageImport where this clause writes ImportDeclaration. This clause does not define a FilterPackageImport, and the rule follows the clause's ImportDeclaration. The clause's ImportDeclaration makes the rule indirectly recursive: ImportDeclaration includes NamespaceImport, whose second alternative is a FilterPackage. So `a::*[x][y]` can parse as one filter package with two members, or as a filter package nested inside another. The token language is the same either way, since a nested filter package only adds more bracketed members. The Earley oracle accepts the ambiguity; a recursive-descent implementation must choose the flat reading. The clause is followed.

evidence.note: FilterPackage : Package = ownedRelationship += ImportDeclaration ( ownedRelationship += FilterPackageMember )+

lines 34-36: `private import DesignModel::**[@Structure] [(as Annotations::ApprovalAnnotation).approved and (as Annotations::ApprovalAnnotation).level > 1];`, a recursive MembershipImport filtered by two members
